column1: # DevCouncil `--json` invocations whose stdout must hold exactly one JSON value.
# Fields are TAB-separated. The first is the mode; the rest are argv, passed to
# the process directly — there is no shell here, so nothing needs quoting. The
# format is `dcjsoncheck`'s, which is what runs this file.
# `{DEVCOUNCIL}` is replaced with the host binary the harness resolved and
# `{ROOT}` with the throwaway git repository it created, so every entry runs
# against a real, freshly-scaffolded project rather than the developer's own
# This list named `{PY} -m devcouncil.cli.main …` until 2026-09-14. That module
# was deleted in 3286db5 when the orchestrator moved to Go, so every invocation
# here had been unrunnable — and the harness skipped instead of failing, which
# is how a gate that ran nothing kept reporting the green of a gate that ran.
# The surviving `--json` CLIs are the Go host and `devmap`; `devmap`'s own
# contract is owned by `rust/devmap-cli/tests/cli_json_contract.rs`, in the
# crate that builds it, so this file is the host's half and does not duplicate
# Both outcomes are covered on purpose: a command that succeeds and a command
# that rejects its arguments owe stdout the same one object. The host keeps
# that promise in one place — `console.Session.Finish` emits
# `{"ok":false,"diagnostics":[…]}` when `--json` was asked for and no handler
# wrote a payload — so a rejecting path that prints only to stderr is a real
# regression, not an accepted shape. Every entry below was run against
# dea408e; the `hook status --client` pair failed there and is the reason this
# Nothing here may write to the project or the developer's machine: `install`
# only ever appears with `--dry-run` (or a name that fails to resolve), and
# --- gate: the smallest read, and the presentation seam around it --------------
# `--progress always` forces the live renderer on while `--json` is set; it
# must still render to stderr. That interaction is the one this file exists to
# hold, and it is invisible to any in-process test of the handler.
# `gate set` has no --json of its own, so this is the unknown-flag refusal on a
# --json argv: the envelope owes stdout an object even for a flag nobody parsed.
# --- install: the receipt, the dry-run plan, and the refusals ------------------
# --- integrate: the receipt path, and the two refusals that carry none ---------
# `--write-gate` is refused by name rather than as an unknown flag, and that
# branch returns before `integrate.Run`, so nothing writes a receipt.
# --- hook: the retired lifecycle surface's two management subcommands ----------
# `--client nosuchhost` is refused inside `integrate.Uninstall`, which returns
# no receipt. Both of these left stdout empty at dea408e, because `hook` took
# the protocol path and so never reached the envelope in `Finish`. They are the
# entries that fail against the pre-fix host.
